title: Pacote de Evidência de Model-Risk — Bridge Banking AI
note: Hash de conteúdo determinístico (sha256) sobre o pacote canônico — reproduzível e verificável; não é assinatura PKI. Consistente com a cadeia de auditoria tamper-evident da demo. Backend fake (sem dados reais).

model_card.title: Model Card — Bridge Banking AI

identity.name: Bridge Banking AI
identity.type: Pipeline de LLM com guard de incerteza (intenção → RAG → agente → guard)

intended_use.purpose: Triagem de atendimento bancário: classifica a intenção do cliente, fundamenta a resposta em documentos (RAG) e libera apenas respostas com confiança suficiente — o resto é sinalizado ou escalado a um humano.
intended_use.users: Equipe de atendimento do banco; a demo expõe a visão de observabilidade e governança.
intended_use.in_scope: 24 intenções em 3 famílias: bancário, fraude e segurança.
out_of_scope: Execução real de transações (PIX, TED, pagamentos) — a demo nunca movimenta dinheiro.
Decisão de crédito, investimento ou aconselhamento financeiro.
Substituir o atendente humano em fraude, crise ou alto risco (sempre escala).

architecture.name: Pipeline
architecture.detail: 12 estágios: dq_input → data_governance → cache → complexity → memory → RAG → intent → agent → guard → cache_store → dq_output → audit.

architecture.name: Classificador de intenção
architecture.detail: 24 intenções (bancário / fraude / segurança), confiança por palavras-chave.

architecture.name: Agentes
architecture.detail: 3 agentes registrados (chatbot, smart_payments, call_center) com handoffs.

architecture.name: RAG
architecture.detail: Recuperação TF-IDF real sobre 5 documentos pré-carregados.

architecture.name: Guard de incerteza
architecture.detail: Limiar runtime 0.70; decide PASSTHROUGH / FLAG / REASK / ESCALATE.

controls.name: Guard de incerteza
controls.detail: Toda resposta passa pelo guard (estágio 9); fraude e segurança sempre escalam, independente da confiança.

controls.name: Auditoria tamper-evident
controls.detail: Cadeia hash sha256 (prev_hash ‖ payload) registra cada decisão; verify/replay detectam edição silenciosa.

controls.name: Data Governance (LGPD)
controls.detail: Mascaramento de PII (cartão, CPF, passaporte) antes de persistir na auditoria.

controls.name: Data Quality
controls.detail: 16 regras de entrada (incl. bloqueio de prompt-injection) + 4 de saída.

controls.name: Drift detection
controls.detail: TV-distance entre baseline e janela atual; rebaseline manual ou automático.

controls.name: Crosswalk SR 11-7
controls.detail: Mapeia os 3 pilares (Conceptual Soundness, Outcome Analysis, Ongoing Monitoring) — ver painel Conformidade SR 11-7.

limitations: Backend padrão é o FakeBackend (respostas pré-definidas, sem LLM real, sem dados bancários reais).
Calibração (ECE/Brier/AUROC) é calculada de verdade sobre as amostras rotuladas do catálogo; não há benchmark de produção do backend fake, então os demais alvos do SR 11-7 ficam sintéticos/pendentes.
Personas e corpus RAG são pré-semeados (MOCK); a recuperação TF-IDF roda de verdade sobre eles.
Persistência em SQLite (demo); datas de revisão de governança abaixo são ilustrativas.

governance.status: Demo controlada — gaps documentados em DEMO_SCOPE.md.
governance.evidence: Versão / prompt / corpus fixados por fingerprint e cruzáveis com os timestamps da auditoria.

calibration.title: Calibração do classificador de intenção
calibration.source: Consultas de exemplo rotuladas do catálogo de intenções (lub.calibration).
calibration.method: Para cada (consulta, intenção esperada) do catálogo, classify_intent → (predito, confiança); acerto = predito==esperado. Métricas reais via lub: ECE (Guo 2017), Brier, AUROC de recusa, sharpness e a reliability curve.
calibration.honesty: Calibração calculada de verdade sobre as consultas rotuladas do catálogo (amostras semeadas, não tráfego de produção) — os mesmos números do pilar Outcome Analysis do SR 11-7. A confiança do classificador é heurística (níveis discretos), então a curva é esparsa; produção usaria logprobs de token.

controls.description: Circular 3.978, Art. 3: Assegurar qualidade, integridade e rastreabilidade dos dados. Proveniencia de dataset (hash, versao) e calibracao por grupo demografico atendem este artigo.

Art. 5: Instituicoes devem implementar e manter politica de gestao de riscos de tecnologia proporcional ao porte e complexidade das operacoes. Metricas de incerteza (ECE, AUROC de recusa) evidenciam avaliacao continua de risco.
Art. 7: Monitorar continuamente os riscos de tecnologia e tomar acoes corretivas tempestivas. Cobertura conformal adaptativa e PRR fornecem monitoramento quantificado.

Section V.A: Evaluate the design and theoretical foundation of the model. Reviewers expect quantitative evidence that predicted probabilities match observed outcomes -- ECE, RMSCE, ENCE, Brier, miscalibration area, sharpness, Spearman/Kendall rank correlation, and adversarial-group calibration all provide this evidence.

Section V.B: Evaluate the model's performance against its intended outcomes including task accuracy and the model's ability to identify its own failures. Accuracy, Matthews correlation, refusal AUROC, PRR, reversed-pairs proportion, AURC, and AUUCC provide outcome-analysis evidence.

Section VI.A: Document the model lifecycle so an independent reviewer can reproduce results -- dataset provenance, code revisions, dependency versions. dataset_hash, dataset_version, git_sha, and package_versions provide reproducible documentation. Auto-bot commits in regulated code paths must remain attributable (see MODEL_INVENTORY.md in n8n_scripts/).

Section VI.B: Monitor model performance on an ongoing basis -- abstention rates, drift detection, dependency fingerprinting. missing_ratio and adaptive conformal coverage provide ongoing-monitoring evidence. Production deployments wire these into the Bridge AuditTrail (lub.connectors.bridge.audit).

Section VI.C: Independent review of model development by parties not involved in the development. Git history with auto-bot vs human attribution (.mailmap), append-only audit ledger of every customer-facing AI output (lub.connectors.bridge.audit), and quality gates (mypy / bandit / pytest / coverage) on every auto-bot commit provide audit-defensible records.

frameworks.title: NIST AI 600-1 Generative AI Profile of AI RMF 1.0

controls.description: MG-4.1: Maintain change-management records -- code revisions, dependency versions, configuration drift -- for GenAI systems (NIST AI 600-1 SS MG-4.1).
MS-2.11: Evaluate group-conditional performance and coverage guarantees (e.g. Mondrian conformal) to detect disparate impact in GenAI outputs (NIST AI 600-1 SS MS-2.11).
MS-2.3: Assess AI system performance including accuracy on domain-specific evaluation sets, with documentation of methods, metrics, and results (NIST AI 600-1 SS MS-2.3).

MS-2.5: Quantify and report prediction confidence and uncertainty bounds for generative AI outputs, ensuring that uncertainty information is available for downstream decisions (NIST AI 600-1 SS MS-2.5).
MS-2.6: Evaluate calibration of confidence estimates against observed outcomes; report ECE, reliability curves, and scoring rules (NIST AI 600-1 SS MS-2.6).
MS-2.7: Measure the AI system's ability to safely abstain or refuse when confidence is insufficient, using refusal AUROC and selective-prediction metrics (NIST AI 600-1 SS MS-2.7).
MS-2.8: Maintain provenance records for datasets, model versions, and evaluation configurations to support reproducibility (NIST AI 600-1 SS MS-2.8).
MS-2.9: Evaluate robustness of AI outputs under distribution shift, including adaptive conformal coverage and temporal calibration stability (NIST AI 600-1 SS MS-2.9).

frameworks.title: BCBS 239 — Principles for effective risk data aggregation and risk reporting

controls.description: Principle 1: Develop models based on sound theory and appropriate data. Evaluation-set metrics, dataset provenance, and calibration evidence satisfy P1 documentation requirements.
Principle 3: Conduct effective model validation using independent quantitative testing. ECE, Brier, AURC, and adversarial-group-calibration are P3 validation tests.
Principle 5: Monitor model performance on an ongoing basis. Adaptive conformal coverage, PRR trending, and ensemble disagreement provide continuous-monitoring evidence.
SS 6.3: Perform AI risk assessment including identification, analysis, and evaluation. ECE, Brier, miscalibration area, and adversarial-group-calibration implement risk analysis.
SS 6.4: Implement risk treatment controls. Refusal policies (UALA gated tool call), abstention thresholds, and conformal prediction sets implement treatment strategies.
SS 6.5: Record and report risk management activities. OSCAL Component Definitions and Assessment Results provide machine-readable reporting artifacts.
SS 6.6: Monitor and review the AI risk management framework. Adaptive conformal coverage, temporal PRR, and UCC/AUUCC provide ongoing monitoring evidence.
SS 8.2: Manage the AI system lifecycle -- design, development, deployment, monitoring, and retirement -- with documented evidence at each stage.
SS 8.4: Operate AI systems with appropriate monitoring, incident response, and performance tracking. Adaptive conformal coverage and PRR provide operational evidence.
SS 9.1: Monitor, measure, analyse and evaluate the AI management system and AI system performance. ECE, Brier, AURC, and calibration metrics implement this clause.
A.5.4: Manage data used in AI systems to ensure quality, integrity, and traceability. Dataset provenance (hash, version) and adversarial-group-calibration provide evidence.
A.6.2.4: Define and implement lifecycle processes for AI systems including version control, dependency management, and change tracking. Git SHA and package versions provide evidence.
A.6.2.6: Evaluate and document AI system performance including accuracy, calibration, and scoring-rule metrics on representative evaluation sets.
A.7.3: Implement operational controls for AI systems including refusal mechanisms, selective prediction, and continuous monitoring of performance under production conditions.

Art. 10: Ensure training, validation and testing data are relevant, representative, and free of errors. Dataset provenance, hashing, and adversarial-group-calibration metrics address Art. 10(2)(f) on bias examination.
Art. 13: Ensure AI systems are transparent enough for deployers to interpret outputs. Uncertainty reporting, confidence bounds, and reliability diagrams satisfy Art. 13(3)(b)(ii) disclosure.
Art. 14: Enable human oversight of the AI system. Refusal AUROC, abstention rates, and gated tool-call policies (UALA) implement Art. 14(4)(a) real-time intervention capability.
Art. 15(1): Achieve appropriate levels of accuracy for the intended purpose. Task accuracy, Brier scores, and proper scoring rules provide evidence.
Art. 15(4): Be resilient to errors, faults, and inconsistencies in input data. Adaptive conformal coverage, miscalibration area, and AURC under shift measure robustness.

Art. 9: Establish, implement, document and maintain a risk management system throughout the AI system's lifecycle. LUB metrics (ECE, AURC, PRR) provide the quantitative risk evidence required by Art. 9(2)(a).

Section V.A: Evaluate the design and theoretical foundation of the model. Reviewers expect quantitative evidence that predicted probabilities match observed outcomes -- ECE, RMSCE, ENCE, Brier, miscalibration area, sharpness, Spearman/Kendall rank correlation, and adversarial-group calibration all provide this evidence.
